 Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham

 James Maddison isn't happy but it's all from the Cole Palmer free kick, the pressure. 
 Chelsea did this at Arsenal didn't they, leaving four up and Spurs have reacted.

 'Spurs need a good performance' published at 17:34 BST 17:34 BST 
 Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham 
 Gary Neville 
Former Manchester United defender on Sky Sports 
 Tottenham getting a decent performance against Manchester United and a win against Coventry on Monday night was a big one for them. 
 They don't have a good record at Stamford Bridge but they need a good performance. 
 63 33 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'The reward we were looking for' published at 17:33 BST 17:33 BST 
 FT: Coventry 0-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa speaking to BBC MOTD: 
 "We have the reward we were looking for. We competed for 90 minutes and tried to play our game. It wasn't easy, tough team and we knew it. But we did really well. The last victory away from home was too many months ago so this was important for us.
 "Another clean sheet, massive for us. We have the quality and players to score goals but we need to press well, defend well in the Premier League and it's so difficult. You can feel that they can score if you lose concentration and we did really well."
 On Oscar Bobb goal: "We need his goals, Josh's [King] goals, they are people that play in front and our attacking players are so important. They need to make the difference. They are young players and the most difficult thing in football is goals but they are working hard and improving. He's doing well and needs to keep going.
 "The best last touch in a game!"
 9 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Quenda is playing on the left side of Chelsea's attack published at 17:33 BST 17:33 BST 
 Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport senior football reporter 
 Surprise selection Geovany Quenda is starting on the left side of attack as Chelsea kick off, Morgan Rogers striker, as expected, and Cole Palmer on the right.
 Reminder: Joao Pedro is out through injury and will be assessed.

 get involved Get Involved published at 17:33 BST 17:33 BST 
 Use 'Get involved' to have your say 
 So instead of Estevao or Welbeck both who have played in the Premier League Alsono picks Quenda who has never played a game in the PL? He must really have a grudge against Estavao to not pick him today.
 Spencer, London 
 Wow Estevao has clearly done something to annoy Alonso.
 Mills, Brighton

 Post published at 17:32 BST 17:32 BST 
 Chelsea 0-0 Tottenham 
 This is just the sixth Premier League campaign neither Chelsea or Spurs are playing in Europe, and just second of the 21st century after 2023-24. 
 The Blues are unbeaten in 10 meetings with Spurs when neither have European football (W6 D4)

 KICK-OFF published at 17:31 BST 17:31 BST

 Off we go in this London derby.

 The weather is atrocious at this London derby published at 17:30 BST 17:30 BST 
 Chelsea v Tottenham (17:30 BST) 
 Nizaar Kinsella 
BBC Sport senior football reporter 
 Heavy rain has been falling continuously for several hours in west London as Storm Boelo sweeps across the capital.
 The grounds staff have been doing all they can to keep the pitch in suitable condition and were still out there poking the surface with pitchforks as the teams emerged.
 The slick surface will no doubt have an impact on the type of match we see.
 Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso called on his players to show "emotional control" while maintaining the passion required for a match of this magnitude at Stamford Bridge.
 56 9 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Didn't do enough in attacking sense' published at 17:30 BST 17:30 BST 
 FT: Arsenal 2-0 Everton 
 Everton 
 Everton manager David Moyes, speaking to BBC Match of the Day: "[Going 1-0 down early] made it hard and we couldn't really get ourselves back into the game after that.
 "Huffed and puffed a little bit, stuck at it for long parts of the game, which was good. We never gave them anything easy but, in the end, we didn't have enough."
 On Arsenal's first goal: "I need to see it again but I know it was a little bit scruffy at the back post. We didn't quite clear it or get a touch on it. But, apart from that, we defended pretty well from most [set pieces]."
 On Jake O'Brien and Tyrique George: "I thought they both did well today, they both played well. I thought a lot of the players did a good job today.
 "We didn't do enough in an attacking sense but we certainly did a really good job defensively, try to make it difficult.
 "But we really wanted to score some goals. We had a couple of chances, Thierno [Barry] in the first half and then a bit unlucky with Keirnan [Dewsbury-Hall] late in the game. But we certainly need to do that better than we did today."
 On why he was booked: "I don't know. I felt for [the referee] today because I thought he was really poor, so I felt for him."
 10 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Tough week but we have to continue' published at 17:30 BST 17:30 BST 
 FT: Coventry 0-1 Fulham 
 Coventry City 
 Coventry manager Frank Lampard speaking to BBC MOTD: 
 "Disappointed to lose. Can't stand here and say we should have won. A tight game without big chances for either team. We wanted to get a point out of the game we know all thee games are to9ugh. We weren't threatened too much. We didn't threaten them enough to give ourselves a chance of winning the game but then you just don't want to lose. Fair play it took a moment of quality from them to get the goal but disappointed to lose."
 On Fulham's goal: "Good players when they stand you up in the box, he shifts it finds the small area that can give him a goal. Disappointed but also a moment of quality."
 On Bobby Thomas injury: "We hope not too serious. I don't know the extent of the injury. He played some sickness but we hope it's only a small injury.
 "This season is going to be tough and we have to be robust and stay resilient in these moments. Tough week but we have to continue."

 LINE-UPS published at 17:27 BST 17:27 BST 
 Chelsea v Tottenham (17:30 BST) 
 The players are coming out on to the pitch. Here's a reminder of the teams, with Chelsea without the injured Joao Pedro.

 'Slightly off our usual selves' published at 17:25 BST 17:25 BST 
 FT: Coventry 0-1 Fulham 
 Coventry City 
 Coventry manager Frank Lampard speaking to Sky Sports: 
 "They're a good team and there wasn't much in it at both boxes. Throughout the game very limited chances, we defended well but they didn't open us up really but neither did we. Then we conceded the goal with a moment of quality from them which we couldn't produce.
 "There's always things you can do the quality of the finish is good. We can analyse to see where we can do better.
 "It [reaction] has to be good - this is the story of this league. Trying to compete, the gap is what it is. Couple of games where the result hasn't come and a couple where it has. We want to try and win games but if we don't win we don't want to lose.
 "We have to be realistic, have to be maxed out every week. Fully prepared and fully positive and we weren't quite that today we were slightly off our usual selves. You can suffer in games like this but you have to try and turn that."
 16 7 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'I worry for Coventry' published at 17:23 BST 17:23 BST 
 FT: Coventry 0-1 Fulham 
 Chris Sutton 
Former Celtic striker on Final Score 
 I tipped Coventry for relegation at the start of the season. I'm not going to change that, I just worry for them. 
 You look at other teams that have come up like Hull City, and Ipswich, they're making a fist of it. I see Ipswich with a better balance of play than what Coventry do. 
 That was a big game for them today, had Frank Lampard got it over the line, but I think it's a big win for Fulham and Alvaro Arbeloa.
 27 14 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'We expect a good support for the team' published at 17:21 BST 17:21 BST 
 Chelsea v Tottenham (17:30 BST) 
 Chelsea 
 Xabi Alonso called on Chelsea supporters to generate an “electric energy” when Tottenham visit Stamford Bridge. The fierce rivals meet for the first time since Alonso took charge in the summer with the hosts going into the game seven points and 12 places above Spurs.
 Back-to-back victories, 5-1 against Bournemouth and 2-0 at Everton, have been built on much greater organisation after a chaotic start, and the Blues start as strong favourites to make it three wins in a row, despite Roberto De Zerbi’s team finally getting off the mark by beating Coventry on Monday.
 “We’re expecting a good atmosphere, electric with good energy,” said Blues boss Alonso. “Knowing that this passion is really in the air in the stadium, we need to use it in the proper way. This is one of those games where that excitement is something that you need. You don’t need extra motivation because that will come naturally, because of the history of the derby. It’s a top game.”
 Mike Penders, who became the club’s youngest Premier League goalkeeper when he replaced the injured Emiliano Martinez during the second half of Saturday’s win on Merseyside, will make his full league debut after Martinez had surgery on a fractured jaw.
 “We expect a good support for the team and for Mike,” added Alonso. “We need that connection with the crowd, in good moments, tough moments. For me it’s fundamental we play our game on the pitch, the players do their best.
 “When the crowd is living it. That’s the good thing about the Premier League. The crowd plays the game as well, it’s not that they just watch the game. Spontaneously some energy is created in this league. It’s a big boost for the team.”
 31 13 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A good, clear step forward' published at 17:19 BST 17:19 BST 
 FT: Aston Villa 2-1 Man City 
 Aston Villa 
 Aston Villa manager Unai Emery, speaking to TNT Sports: "We planned this match trying to keep the same consistency and demands. How we responded with some players fresh who didn't play on Wednesday.
 "It was a match for them - for example Boubacar Kamara and Matty Cash. This is the level we want to keep achieving through our high demands. Today was a good test. We were very motivated and I was o excited for this test to face them.
 "Progressively we are getting better, structure is stronger and subs had a good impact. A good, clear step forward."
 On Nicolas Jackson: "How he was working, defending, getting duels - wow. He has the power to attack with spaces, duels and his challenge has been when he has chances to score always in the corner in the goal.
 "At the beginning of the season he was shooting so much as though he was playing rugby, so he is progressing as well. He is doing his tasks."
 On progress: "We are progressing but we are under our expectation from the beginning of the season because we started so poorly. Now we are progressing. We analysed the match against Forest and our performance was so bad.
 "We improved a lot of things against Brentford at home, we were better but not enough. Today, everything we were working to improve to set our standards high, today was a step forward. Champions League we are performing fantastic. In the league we are progressing but still under our expectations.
 "The objective is to compete with these teams - City and Arsenal."
 52 4 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Don't see Spurs getting anything' published at 17:18 BST 17:18 BST 
 Chelsea v Tottenham (17:30 BST) 
 Image source, BBC Sport We were talking on the Monday Night Club about what Chelsea could do this season without any European football.
 Tottenham are not in Europe either, of course, but they don't look like they are going to be challenging at the top of the table the way Xabi Alonso's side are.
 People keep saying how Chelsea's attack is so good, but their 2-0 win over Everton last time out was their first clean sheet of their campaign in the league, and that side of thing still needs to improve.
 Spurs, meanwhile, do seem to be getting better, albeit slowly.
 It was a big result for them to beat Coventry on Monday but they have an awful record at Stamford Bridge, with only one win there in the Premier League era.
 I don't see them getting anything this time, either.
 Sutton's prediction: 3-1
 50 40 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Spurs aim to improve poor record against Chelsea published at 17:17 BST 17:17 BST 
 Chelsea v Tottenham (17:30 BST) 
 Tottenham Hotspur 
 Roberto De Zerbi has insisted Tottenham will use their horrible record at Chelsea as motivation and not allow it to build pressure before their London derby.
 Spurs have claimed only one victory at Stamford Bridge in the Premier League era and lost 10 of the past 12 meetings between the rival clubs. However, De Zerbi was quick to shut down any suggestions Tottenham’s poor form in this derby will add pressure and instead backed his players to build on Monday’s 3-1 home win over Coventry.
 Asked if he sensed any fear in his squad, De Zerbi said: “No. I think no because I play just one game with Chelsea as Tottenham coach. Anyway, it has to be one motivation more. Not one more problem for us.
 “What is the problem? We didn’t play in the past for Tottenham and I was not the Tottenham coach in the last seasons. It is not a problem. We have already many problems and this is not a problem. I think it’s not just this negative record. There are many, many negative records, but for me it’s one motivation more.
 “For the players, I want this negative record, they give us more motivation, more mentality, more energy to win a game, to play a good game, because we have the qualities enough to win. Yes, it’s a derby against one very good team, very good coach, they have a clear style of play, great players, but also Tottenham players are very good.
 “The level of the (Tottenham) players is high. We have to show together as a team, not as an individual.”
 29 21 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'A big three points for Arsenal' published at 17:16 BST 17:16 BST 
 FT: Arsenal 2-0 Everton 
 Chris Sutton 
Former Celtic striker on Final Score 
 It's about squad depth and Arsenal have shown today changes which they've made, with Bukayo Saka being injured and out for a while, but they have players who can come in and may not be as effective but still enough to get over the line. A big three points. 
 80 25 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'This is the way we have to play' published at 17:15 BST 17:15 BST 
 FT: Coventry 0-1 Fulham 
 Fulham 
 Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa speaking to Sky Sports: 
 "So happy - again a very good game for us in a difficult stadium. Another clean sheet. We competed really well, tried to play our football. Not an easy game but we did well, scored our goal, controlled the game. Took the ball and controlled for the last 10 minutes. We ran, pressed and this is what we want - very happy."
 On Oscar Bobb goal: "Young player and for me as a coach it would be easier to sign players with experience but they have the talent and I trust them. They are the people and the future of Fulham. Happy with this young talent.
 "We are working so hard every day and we need to be at our best every day. We started to prepare this game at the beginning of the week. It's important to involve every player in the squad, players from the bench did well. So happy with everyone and this is the way we have to play."
 On Tom Cairney: "Amazing - he is our captain and when Tom is playing I ask everyone to give the ball to Tom. We need his talent and his experience."
 On possible penalty: "No questions about referees please."
 33 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Been waiting for my first goal' published at 17:12 BST 17:12 BST 
 FT: Arsenal 2-0 Everton 
 Arsenal 
 Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa, speaking to PLP: "Great feeling, it always is. A clean sheet, a goal - my first goal for the club - so a fantastic day overall."
 On his goal: "I've been waiting to score my first goal for a while. I spoke to the set piece coach before the game and he told me he's been waiting for my goal as well, so it was only right that I got the goal today."
 On if Arsenal set-piece goal was coming: "Yeah, definitely after the game against Bayern, where we created a few chances with our set pieces.
 "We felt as players that it was coming and today was the day."
 On Gabriel scoring on his 200th Premier League appearance: "Very pleased for him. He's a top, top player. Top human being. Very happy for him. He's my life easy since I've joined the club and it's been a pleasure playing alongside him."
 On good form at Emirates: "I've come to this stadium for many seasons, I know how tough it is to play against us. It's not surprising to me.
 "We are champions and to be champions you've got to win games consistently. This is our home and we want to win as many games here as possible."
